h2: Water Leak Repair Jimbaran – Finding & Fixing Hidden Leaks
intro: If your PDAM meter keeps creeping or a pump cycles on and off with no visible drip, water leak repair in Jimbaran is usually the next step before hidden moisture reaches walls, floors or foundations. Salt air along the bay and hard water up the Bukit mean fittings degrade faster here than in most parts of Bali, so small seeps can quietly become structural problems.

sections.h3: Why Jimbaran's Setting Makes Leaks Sneakier
sections.text: Villas along Kedonganan and Jimbaran Bay sit close enough to salt air that brass fittings, pump seals and even PVC joints corrode a few seasons earlier than inland. Up toward Bukit Jimbaran, gravity works against you: tanks and booster pumps run harder, pressure swings stress every connection, and hard water leaves scale inside mixers and heater coils. A drip that would be obvious in a flat compound can hide for weeks behind a stucco wall up the hill.

sections.h3: The Jobs We See Most Around Here
sections.text: The most common calls break down into a handful of patterns: a slow seep under a kitchen or bathroom sink, a shower tray or floor drain that never quite stops trickling, a burst PPR pipe behind a feature wall, and irrigation lines in the garden that flood one patch while another stays dry. Family villas with pools add another layer—more bathrooms, bigger circulation loops, and more points where a gasket can fail silently.

sections.h3: What to Send on WhatsApp for a Quote
sections.text: Send a short video or a few clear photos on WhatsApp: the PDAM meter reading over time if it's creeping, the area where you notice dampness or a musty smell, any visible corrosion on fittings, and the pump or tank setup if pressure is involved. If you're not sure what to photograph, just describe what you see and where. Pricing depends entirely on the job—access, materials, whether it's behind a wall or exposed—so we'll give you a firm figure after reviewing your photos.

sections.h3: Keeping Fittings Alive in This Climate
sections.text: Flush water heaters and mixers every six months so scale doesn't trap moisture inside. Inspect outdoor fittings and pump connections near the bay for white salt residue each dry season. Keep track of how often your booster pump cycles—if it's kicking in more frequently, something upstream is losing pressure. After the first heavy rains of wet season, walk the garden irrigation lines once; joints that held fine through dry heat can shift and start weeping as soil swells.

faq.q: How do you locate a leak when there's no visible drip?
faq.a: We trace the supply line from the meter, check pressure at each branch, and use targeted testing around suspect walls or floors to isolate the exact joint or pipe section before opening anything up.

faq.q: Can you handle leaks behind stucco or feature walls in a villa?
faq.a: Yes—once the source is isolated, we open only the smallest access point needed, swap out the failed section with the correct fitting, and test under full pressure before closing up.

faq.q: Do pool plumbing leaks fall under this service too?
faq.a: If the issue sits in the circulation loop, filter housing gaskets, or return lines tied into your main water supply, yes—we cover those within the same leak-diagnosis process.
